newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares seen rebounding, IPOs to start trade.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares seen rebounding, IPOs to start trade.

text.p: Shares are expected to see some rebound on Wednesday after a short consolidation period on Tuesday to gather energy, brokers said.
Four initial public offerings, including Hyundai Housing and AUK Corp, will begin trading today.

"The market fell yesterday but we don't see that as unhealthy," said market analyst Lee Sang-koo of Hyundai Securities. "Sentiment is still good, customer deposits are growing and hopes of an interest rate cut is keeping investors focused." The composite stock index lost 13.67 points to close at 828.61.

Four offerings will begin their debut trading on Tuesday. Hyundai Housing will see 6.2 million shares trade, transistor maker AUK Corp, 500,000 shares, Dong Yang Elevator, 600,000, and Korea Electronic Terminal, 280,000.
"AUK Corp is the most interesting of the four because it is related to telecommunications equipment," said Lee.
The Securities Exchange Commission is expected to make an announcement on Wednesday about a probe into price manipulation and insider trading cases, brokers said.
